answer: An agent network can deter Sybil attacks using optical physical unclonable functions. Nodes register by scattering light through a physical token containing dispersed pigment and a quartz crystal matrix, producing unique responses that seed an identity cipher. An adversary incurs the scarce physical cost of fabricating distinct microscopic media for every forged agent. However, thermal drift and sensor degradation can alter optical readouts, causing legitimate agents to fail verification.
